title: Binary polynomial-time membership via an encoded alphabet
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $e$ be an injective map from the binary alphabet into $\Gamma$, let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over $\Gamma$, and let $L$ be a language of binary strings. If, on every binary input $x$, the machine run on the symbolwise image $e(x)$ halts within $C(|x|+1)^d$ steps and outputs the one-symbol string containing $e(1)$ when $x\in L$ and $e(0)$ otherwise, for natural numbers $C,d$, then $L$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$L$ is a language of binary strings
For every binary input, $M$ decides membership in $L$ via $e$ within $C(|x|+1)^d$ steps
replaced:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let
$e : \{0,1\} \hookrightarrow \Gamma$ be an injective embedding of the binary
symbols, let $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$ be a language over the binary alphabet,
and let $C$ and $d$ be natural numbers. If some deterministic finite Turing
machine over $\Gamma$ decides $L$ via $e$ within $C \cdot (n+1)^d$ steps on
every input of length $n$, then $L \in \mathsf{P}$. In particular, polynomial-time
decidability over any finite alphabet already places a language in the
binary-alphabet class $\mathsf{P}$.
